name: HTTP request
description: Calls one HTTP(S) endpoint - GET a JSON config, POST a webhook, poll a status URL - and stores the response as artifacts - status, body, headers, and the body parsed as json when it is JSON. In-process fetch: no curl, no shell quoting, no platform gotchas. No AI involved.

args.name: url
args.label: URL
args.description: http:// or https://, resolved templates and all - what a gate shows is what is called.

args.name: headers
args.label: Headers
args.description: Request headers as a map. Do not put credentials here - point authEnv at the env var holding them instead, so the value is masked everywhere.

args.name: body
args.label: Body
args.description: Sent as-is. Content-Type defaults to application/json when a body is given and no header names one.

args.name: authEnv
args.label: Auth env var
args.description: Env var holding the full Authorization header value, e.g. 'Bearer <token>'. Read under the declaration and registered as a secret - it never lands in a log or the run record.

args.name: timeoutMs
args.label: Timeout (ms)
args.description: Per-request ceiling, so a dead endpoint fails the task rather than hanging it.

args.name: failOnHttpError
args.label: Fail on 4xx/5xx
args.description: true fails the task on a non-2xx status. false stores the status and carries on - for polling, or when a later if: reads run.context.NAME.status.
